title: Orsen and the Deadline
premise: Freya Winterbourne, a hostage negotiator whose one failed negotiation still haunts her, has spent six years living under a polished lie: that she left the covert training network known as the Chalk Line after it burned her partner and her reputation. When a realtor's listing for their remote safe house appears online — complete with interior photos of rooms no outsider should know exist — Freya realizes someone inside the network is hunting them, using the sale as bait. With the summit convening in three weeks, she must team up with Orsen, the handler she once loved and was ordered to betray, to trace the leak through the very people who trained them both. In the end, Freya exposes the Chalk Line's director at the summit by sacrificing her own cover, choosing truth over loyalty, and walks away from Orsen alive but unattached — love against duty resolved in duty's favor, with a door left ajar.
about_author: Ines Delacroix is the pen name of a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to people talk each other back from ledges. She writes thrillers about the moment when words are the only weapon left.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV Freya. A late-night scroll reveals the safe house listed online with photos of the kitchen where she once hid a gun in the flour tin. The beat is cold dread: invisibility was an illusion, and someone curated these images deliberately.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Rules
chapters.summary: POV Freya. She wakes Orsen, they run their rehearsed evacuation drill, but he hesitates over a photo of them on the mantel. Emotional beat: the tension between practiced survival and the domestic life they've pretended is real.

chapters.title: Chalk Dust
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. He admits the listing matches a Chalk Line signature — staged interiors used as dead drops. Flashback to training: how recruits learned to read rooms. Beat: guilt, because Orsen trained the person now hunting them.

chapters.title: One Failure on the Board
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Interrogated by her old agency contact Marsh, she lies about knowing the Chalk Line still exists. Flashback to the failed negotiation that killed a hostage named Ilsa. Beat: shame sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Twenty-One Days
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. They map the countdown to the Geneva summit, where the Chalk Line's director, Voss, will be honored publicly. Beat: grim arithmetic — every day of safety traded against evidence.

chapters.title: The Realtor Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Freya. She tracks the listing agent to a shell office and finds a chalk mark on the doorframe — a recruitment signal. Someone wants her found, not caught. Beat: paranoia curdling into strategy.

chapters.title: What We Were Trained For
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. He confesses his role in Freya's betrayal order six years ago; she already knew. The fight is quiet and devastating. Beat: love tested by the truth it was built to survive.

chapters.title: Safe House Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Freya. An intruder trips their perimeter; it's a teenage recruit, Petra, sent as a messenger with Voss's offer: silence for amnesty. Beat: Freya sees her younger self in the girl and refuses the deal.

chapters.title: Burner Country
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. They go dark, moving through coastal motels while Orsen works his old informant web. One contact agrees to talk, then goes silent mid-call. Beat: the network closing around them, loyalty revealed as currency.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Brother
chapters.summary: POV Freya. She seeks out the brother of the hostage she failed, hoping he'll testify about the Chalk Line's role. He slams the door — then slides a USB under it. Beat: unexpected mercy from grief.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The USB contains audio proving Voss ordered the botched negotiation to eliminate a whistleblower. Orsen recognizes his own voice on the tape, complicit. Beat: self-loathing transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Petra Again
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Petra reappears, injured, having been marked for disposal after delivering the message. Freya shelters her against protocol. Beat: maternal instinct versus operational discipline — the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Marsh's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Marsh offers official backing if Freya testifies anonymously — erasing herself again. Orsen argues she should burn bright instead. Beat: the couple divided over whether survival means hiding or standing.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: POV Freya. A meet with the informant goes wrong; it's a trap, and Freya talks her way out using pure negotiation craft, buying a name: Voss's fixer, Callum. Beat: competence as catharsis — the failure avenged in skill.

chapters.title: Callum
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. They corner Callum, once Orsen's best friend, who reveals the summit is also a handover: Voss is selling the network's methods to a private buyer. Beat: betrayal at scale — loyalty was always a product.

chapters.title: What Petra Saw
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Petra decrypts the listing metadata: photos taken from inside the house, meaning a camera was planted during a visit Freya can't remember. Beat: violation — the past literally watching them.

chapters.title: Nineteen Hours
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Final prep: Freya will enter the summit as press credential holder 'Ines Delacroix,' her chosen alias. Rehearsals, goodbyes drafted and unsent. Beat: tenderness compressed by deadline.

chapters.title: The Summit Floor
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Inside Geneva's conference hall, she watches Voss receive applause and begins feeding evidence to two journalists. Beat: controlled terror, the negotiator negotiating her own life.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Confrontation in a service corridor: Voss offers Freya everything — reinstatement, Orsen's cleared record — for silence. She records the offer. Beat: temptation given its full weight before refusal.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: POV Freya. The recording plays across the summit's open channel as security closes in; Petra's testimony lands simultaneously online. Voss falls; the buyer walks. Beat: climax — truth detonating on schedule.

chapters.title: After the Board Clears
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Fallout: hearings, headlines, Freya's failure officially reframed. He waits at a train platform, unsure if she'll come. Beat: humility — love offered without terms this time.

chapters.title: Unlisted
chapters.summary: POV Freya. She boards the train, not to hide but to choose. Final scene: a new house, no listing, curtains open. Beat: resolution — identity reclaimed, loyalty rewritten as truth, love surviving on honest ground.
